pubd1.io: List commonly used protocols and patient monitoring for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
pubd1.q: Bronchial reactivity is assessed by the fall in forced expiratory volume in 1 second after a patient inhales increasing concentrations of which agent?
opts: Albuterol is a short-acting beta-2 agonist that relaxes bronchial smooth muscle; the agent inhaled to provoke and measure reactivity is methacholine.
Ipratropium blocks acetylcholine at muscarinic receptors and causes bronchodilation; reactivity is measured after inhaling increasing concentrations of methacholine.
Cromolyn is a mast cell stabilizer taken before an antigen insult to prevent attacks; the agent used to assess bronchial reactivity is methacholine.
Correct. Bronchial reactivity is assessed by measuring the fall in forced expiratory volume in 1 second after inhaling increasing concentrations of methacholine.

pubd1.io: Identify respiratory drug classes and commonly prescribed drugs for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
pubd1.q: Albuterol, ipratropium and theophylline share which therapeutic approach to asthma?
opts: Removing the trigger or antigen is the approach of the mast cell stabilizers cromolyn and nedocromil; albuterol, ipratropium and theophylline reverse bronchospasm.
Correct. Beta-2 agonists, ipratropium and theophylline all reverse bronchospasm; cromolyn and nedocromil remove the trigger, and steroids control inflammation.
Controlling inflammation is the approach of steroids and lipoxygenase inhibitors; albuterol, ipratropium and theophylline reverse bronchospasm.
Binding circulating immunoglobulin E is how omalizumab controls inflammation; albuterol, ipratropium and theophylline reverse bronchospasm.

pubd1.io: Identify respiratory drug classes and commonly prescribed drugs for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
pubd1.q: Which long-term controller medication is a methylxanthine?
opts: Correct. Theophylline is the methylxanthine among the long-term controllers; it is a nonspecific phosphodiesterase inhibitor with a narrow therapeutic index.
Montelukast is a long-term controller, but it is a leukotriene modifier (an oral leukotriene D4 antagonist), not a methylxanthine; theophylline is.
Cromolyn is a long-term controller of the mast cell stabilizer group, taken before antigen exposure; the methylxanthine is theophylline.
Salmeterol is a long-term controller of the long-acting beta-2 agonist group, never used alone in asthma; the methylxanthine is theophylline.

pubd1.io: Describe absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion of drugs used for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
pubd1.q: Which drug is the intravenous form of theophylline?
opts: Correct. Theophylline is the methylxanthine, and aminophylline is its intravenous form.
Methylprednisolone is a corticosteroid given orally or parenterally in anaphylaxis and asthma exacerbations; the intravenous methylxanthine is aminophylline.
Reslizumab is an anti-interleukin-5 biologic given intravenously, not a methylxanthine; aminophylline is theophylline's intravenous form.
Levalbuterol (Xopenex) is a short-acting beta-2 agonist, not a methylxanthine; aminophylline is theophylline's intravenous form.

pubd1.io: Identify indications for drugs used for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
pubd1.q: How does theophylline compare with long-acting bronchodilators?
opts: More effective but less well tolerated
Theophylline is not more effective: it is both less effective and less well tolerated than long-acting bronchodilators.
Less effective and less well tolerated
Correct. Compared with long-acting bronchodilators, methylxanthines are less effective and less well tolerated, and theophylline has limited use.
Theophylline is neither as effective nor as well tolerated: it is less effective and less well tolerated than long-acting bronchodilators.
Theophylline is not better tolerated: it has a narrow therapeutic index and is both less effective and less well tolerated.

pubd1.io: Summarize side effects and toxic manifestations of respiratory drugs
pubd1.q: Besides convulsions, which danger of high theophylline levels comes from its action as a cardiac stimulant?
opts: Theophylline stimulates the heart rather than slowing it; the cardiac danger of high levels is arrhythmias.
Hypotension is on the beta-2 agonist adverse effect list; theophylline, a cardiac stimulant, causes arrhythmias at high levels.
Correct. Theophylline is a cardiac stimulant, and high levels cause arrhythmias; as a central nervous system stimulant it also causes convulsions.
Pulmonary edema is a consequence of epinephrine overdose; the cardiac danger of high theophylline levels is arrhythmias.

pubd1.io: Summarize side effects and toxic manifestations of respiratory drugs
pubd1.q: Which eye finding is part of anticholinergic toxicity?
opts: Miosis (a small pupil) is the reverse; anticholinergic toxicity dilates the pupil, giving mydriasis and blurry vision.
Decreased red-green discrimination is ethambutol's visual toxicity; anticholinergics cause blurry vision and mydriasis.
Correct. 'Blind as a bat' stands for blurry vision and mydriasis (dilated pupils) in anticholinergic toxicity.
Orange tears, sweat and urine come from rifampin; the anticholinergic eye findings are blurry vision and mydriasis.

pubd1.io: Identify respiratory drug classes and commonly prescribed drugs for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
pubd1.q: Which inhaled bronchodilator is a short-acting beta-2 agonist?
opts: Salmeterol (Serevent) is a long-acting beta-2 agonist that lasts 12 or more hours and must not be used alone for asthma; levalbuterol is short-acting.
Formoterol (Foradil) is a long-acting beta-2 agonist, also found in Symbicort and Dulera; levalbuterol is the short-acting choice here.
Tiotropium (Spiriva) is a long-acting anticholinergic lasting 24 hours or more, not a beta-2 agonist; levalbuterol is a short-acting beta-2 agonist.
Correct. The short-acting beta-2 agonists are albuterol (Proair, Ventolin) and levalbuterol (Xopenex).

pubd1.io: Summarize side effects and toxic manifestations of respiratory drugs
pubd1.q: Which skin finding is part of anticholinergic toxicity?
opts: Urticaria is a rare side effect of anti-immunoglobulin E therapy such as omalizumab; anticholinergic toxicity causes flushing.
Dermal thinning is a side effect of systemic corticosteroids; the anticholinergic skin finding is flushing.
Diaphoresis (sweating) is an adverse effect of epinephrine; anticholinergic toxicity causes dry mouth and dry eyes with flushing.
Correct. 'Red as a beet' stands for flushing in anticholinergic toxicity, along with fever and hyperthermia ('hot as Hades').

pubd1.io: Describe absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion of drugs used for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
pubd1.q: Which drug works rapidly and lasts about 4 to 6 hours?
opts: Salmeterol is a long-acting beta-2 agonist that lasts 12 or more hours; the rapid, 4-to-6-hour drug is albuterol.
Tiotropium is a long-acting anticholinergic that lasts 24 hours or more; albuterol is the rapid drug that lasts 4 to 6 hours.
Correct. Short-acting beta-2 agonists such as albuterol work rapidly and last 4 to 6 hours, which suits quick relief.
Formoterol is a long-acting beta-2 agonist lasting 12 or more hours; albuterol is the short-acting one, lasting 4 to 6 hours.

pubd1.io: Describe the molecular mechanism of action of drugs used for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
pubd1.q: Besides inhibiting phosphodiesterase, which receptor action is part of theophylline's mechanism?
opts: Muscarinic receptor blockade is the anticholinergic mechanism of ipratropium and tiotropium; theophylline antagonizes adenosine receptors.

Correct. Theophylline inhibits phosphodiesterase (4 and 5), raising cyclic adenosine and guanosine monophosphate, antagonizes the adenosine A2B receptor, and has anti-inflammatory actions in the late response.
Beta-2 receptor stimulation is how albuterol and salmeterol raise cyclic adenosine monophosphate; theophylline is an adenosine receptor antagonist.
Leukotriene D4 receptor blockade is montelukast's mechanism; theophylline antagonizes the adenosine A2B receptor.

pubd1.io: Identify contraindications for drugs used for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
pubd1.q: Which restriction applies to long-acting beta-2 agonists in asthma?
opts: They must not be used alone
Correct. Long-acting beta-2 agonists (formoterol, salmeterol) are not to be used alone for asthma; the combination inhalers pair each with an inhaled corticosteroid.
They must be taken before exposure
Taking a drug before the antigen insult is the rule for the mast cell stabilizers cromolyn and nedocromil; long-acting beta-2 agonists must not be used alone.
Plasma level monitoring belongs to theophylline, which has a narrow therapeutic index; long-acting beta-2 agonists must not be used alone in asthma.
Intravenous use is listed for aminophylline and reslizumab, not for formoterol or salmeterol; in asthma, long-acting beta-2 agonists must not be used alone.

pubd1.io: Describe absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion of drugs used for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
pubd1.q: Which bronchodilator lasts 24 hours or more?
opts: Correct. Tiotropium (Spiriva) is the long-acting anticholinergic and lasts 24 hours or more; ipratropium lasts up to 8 hours.
Ipratropium (Atrovent) is the short-acting anticholinergic and lasts up to 8 hours; tiotropium lasts 24 hours or more.
Albuterol is a short-acting beta-2 agonist that works rapidly and lasts 4 to 6 hours; tiotropium lasts 24 hours or more.
Levalbuterol is a short-acting beta-2 agonist lasting 4 to 6 hours; the bronchodilator lasting 24 hours or more is tiotropium.

pubd1.io: Outline appropriate patient education for drugs used for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
pubd1.q: Besides treating bronchospasm with a short-acting beta-2 agonist, what helps prevent acute bronchospasm in asthma?
opts: Routine antibiotics have no listed role in preventing bronchospasm and are not recommended even for acute bronchitis; avoiding allergens and triggers is the measure.
Exercise and cold air both provoke bronchospasm in asthma, so they are triggers to manage rather than a form of prevention; avoid allergens and triggers instead.
Distilled water is itself a provoker of bronchospasm in asthma; prevention means avoiding allergens and asthma triggers.
Correct. Acute bronchospasm is prevented or reversed by avoiding allergens and asthma triggers and by treating with short-term beta-2 agonists.

pubd1.io: Summarize side effects and toxic manifestations of respiratory drugs
pubd1.q: Which central nervous system effect is listed in anticholinergic toxicity?
opts: Correct. 'Mad as a hatter' stands for hallucinations, delirium, memory loss and psychosis in anticholinergic toxicity.
Emergence phenomenon is an adverse reaction to ketamine, used in status asthmaticus when the patient is intubated; anticholinergics cause delirium and hallucinations.
Euphoria is on isoniazid's central nervous system list with seizures; the anticholinergic list is hallucinations, delirium, memory loss and psychosis.
Insomnia is listed for beta-2 agonists and theophylline; anticholinergic toxicity causes hallucinations, delirium, memory loss and psychosis.

pubd1.io: Describe adverse effects of drugs used for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
pubd1.q: Which combination of heart rate and blood pressure changes is listed among the adverse effects of beta-2 agonists?
opts: Tachycardia with hypertension is the anticholinergic pattern ('the heart runs alone') and an epinephrine effect; beta-2 agonists list tachycardia with hypotension.
Beta-2 agonists speed the heart rather than slow it: they list tachycardia, together with hypotension.
Both directions are reversed: beta-2 agonists list tachycardia and hypotension among their adverse effects.
Correct. The beta-2 agonist adverse effects are tachycardia, hypotension, headache, dizziness, insomnia, tremors and hyperglycemia.

pubd1.io: Describe the molecular mechanism of action of drugs used for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
pubd1.q: Which type of inflammation of the bronchial mucosa characterizes asthma?
opts: Neutrophils join the late asthmatic reaction, releasing proteases and platelet-activating factor, but the inflammation that characterizes asthma is eosinophilic.
Correct. Asthma is widespread, reversible narrowing of the bronchial airways with eosinophilic inflammation of the bronchial mucosa and a marked increase in bronchial responsiveness.
Granulomatous inflammation is not how asthma is described; asthma is eosinophilic inflammation of the bronchial mucosa, with thickening of that mucosa.
T lymphocytes release interleukin-4 and interleukin-5 in the asthmatic reaction, but the mucosal inflammation that characterizes asthma is eosinophilic.

pubd1.io: Outline appropriate patient education for drugs used for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
opts: Allergens trigger fewer attacks than people expect: most asthma attacks are not triggered by allergens but by a viral respiratory infection.
Cold air can provoke bronchospasm, as can exercise, distilled water and rapid respiratory maneuvers, but most attacks follow a viral respiratory infection.
Correct. Most asthma attacks are not triggered by allergens; most are triggered by viral respiratory infection.
Aspirin-induced asthma is a recognized form (montelukast is effective in it), but most asthma attacks are triggered by a viral respiratory infection.

pubd2.io: Identify indications for drugs used for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
pubd2.q: Which drug group is used to reverse acute bronchospasm in asthma?
opts: Inhaled corticosteroids inhibit the inflammatory cascade and take up to 8 weeks for maximal effect; acute bronchospasm is reversed with short-acting beta-2 agonists.
Mast cell stabilizers must be taken before the antigen insult and may take up to 4 weeks to work; acute bronchospasm calls for a short-acting beta-2 agonist.
Leukotriene modifiers such as montelukast are long-term controller medications; acute bronchospasm is reversed with a short-acting beta-2 agonist.
Correct. Acute bronchospasm is prevented by avoiding triggers and reversed with short-acting beta-2 agonists, which work rapidly and last 4 to 6 hours.

pubd2.io: Describe the molecular mechanism of action of drugs used for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
pubd2.q: Beta-2 agonists relax airway smooth muscle by increasing which intracellular messenger?
opts: Cyclic guanosine monophosphate rises, with cyclic adenosine monophosphate, when theophylline inhibits phosphodiesterase; beta-2 agonists act by increasing cyclic adenosine monophosphate.
Correct. Beta-2 agonists increase cyclic adenosine monophosphate, which inhibits myosin light chain kinase and relaxes airway smooth muscle.
Calcium entering through L-type channels or released from the sarcoplasmic reticulum binds calmodulin and drives contraction; beta-2 agonists raise cyclic adenosine monophosphate instead.
Acetylcholine acts on muscarinic receptors, which ipratropium blocks to cause bronchodilation; beta-2 agonists act by increasing cyclic adenosine monophosphate.

pubd2.io: Identify respiratory drug classes and commonly prescribed drugs for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
pubd2.q: Besides short-acting beta-2 agonists and systemic corticosteroids, which drug group is a quick-relief asthma medication?
opts: Leukotriene modifiers are long-term controller medications, alongside inhaled corticosteroids and mast cell stabilizers; anticholinergics are for quick relief.
Mast cell stabilizers are long-term controllers that must be taken regularly; the third quick-relief group is the anticholinergics.
Correct. The quick-relief medications are short-acting beta-2 agonists, anticholinergics and systemic corticosteroids.
Methylxanthines such as theophylline are long-term controller medications; anticholinergics are listed among the quick-relief medications.

pubd2.io: Describe the molecular mechanism of action of drugs used for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
pubd2.q: When allergen binds immunoglobulin E on a mast cell, which mediator is released immediately from the granules?
opts: Correct. Granule content release is immediate: histamine, proteases, heparin and tumor necrosis factor. Lipid mediators follow over minutes and cytokines over hours.
Leukotrienes are membrane-derived lipid mediators made over minutes, along with prostaglandins and platelet-activating factor; histamine is released immediately.
Interleukins are cytokines produced over hours; the immediate release from mast cell granules is histamine, proteases, heparin and tumor necrosis factor.
Prostaglandins are lipid mediators made from the cell membrane over minutes; histamine comes out of the granules immediately.

pubd2.io: Summarize side effects and toxic manifestations of respiratory drugs
pubd2.q: At toxic levels, which central nervous system effect of theophylline is the danger?
opts: Theophylline stimulates rather than sedates the central nervous system (insomnia is on its list); at toxic levels the danger is convulsions.
Emergence phenomenon is an adverse reaction to ketamine in status asthmaticus; theophylline toxicity causes convulsions.
Correct. Theophylline is a central nervous system stimulant, and at high levels it causes convulsions; as a cardiac stimulant it also causes arrhythmias.
Peripheral neuritis from pyridoxine deficiency is isoniazid's toxicity; theophylline at toxic levels causes convulsions.

pubd2.io: Identify indications for drugs used for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
pubd2.q: Besides its limited use in asthma, theophylline is used in which condition?
opts: Correct. Theophylline (available only as a generic) has limited use and is used in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
Ventilator-associated pneumonia is a nosocomial pneumonia treated with broad-spectrum antibiotics; theophylline's listed use is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
Acute bronchitis is generally self-limited and gets symptomatic, supportive care; theophylline's listed use is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
Anaphylaxis is treated with epinephrine, fluids, histamine blockers, albuterol and corticosteroids; theophylline is used in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.

pubd2.io: Describe adverse effects of drugs used for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
pubd2.q: Besides tremor and tachycardia, which metabolic adverse effect is listed for beta-2 agonists?
opts: The direction is reversed: beta-2 agonists raise blood sugar, listed as hyperglycemia, an effect systemic corticosteroids share.
Correct. Beta-2 agonist adverse effects are tachycardia, hypotension, headache, dizziness, insomnia, tremors and hyperglycemia.
Raised uric acid is listed for ethambutol and pyrazinamide; the metabolic adverse effect of beta-2 agonists is hyperglycemia.
Hyperthermia ('hot as Hades') belongs to anticholinergic toxicity; beta-2 agonists list hyperglycemia among their adverse effects.

pubd2.io: Identify indications for drugs used for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
pubd2.q: Which drug group reduces the level of bronchial responsiveness in asthma over the long term?
opts: Short-acting beta-2 agonists treat acute bronchospasm; reducing responsiveness long term needs anti-inflammatory agents such as inhaled corticosteroids.
Anticholinergics are quick-relief bronchodilators that block muscarinic receptors; long-term responsiveness is reduced by inhaled corticosteroids.
Histamine H1 blockers relieve the rash, itching and hives of anaphylaxis; long-term bronchial responsiveness is reduced by inhaled corticosteroids.
Correct. Bronchial responsiveness is related to airway inflammation and is reduced long term with anti-inflammatory agents such as inhaled corticosteroids.

pubd2.io: List commonly used protocols and patient monitoring for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
pubd2.q: Why are theophylline plasma levels monitored?
opts: Inducing cytochrome P450 enzymes is rifampin's interaction problem (theophylline is one of the drugs affected); theophylline is watched because of its narrow therapeutic index.
It has a narrow therapeutic index
Correct. Theophylline has a narrow therapeutic index, so plasma levels are monitored; rising levels bring nausea, vomiting and cardiac effects, then seizures and arrhythmias.
Adrenal suppression is a systemic corticosteroid side effect; theophylline levels are monitored because its therapeutic index is narrow.
Up to 8 weeks for maximal effect describes inhaled corticosteroids; theophylline is monitored for its narrow therapeutic index.

pubd2.io: Describe adverse effects of drugs used for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
pubd2.q: Which change involving urine is listed for theophylline?
opts: Urinary retention is part of anticholinergic toxicity; theophylline has a diuretic effect instead.
Orange urine, tears and sweat come from rifampin; theophylline's listed effect on urine is a diuretic effect.
Correct. Theophylline has diuretic effects, alongside gastric acid stimulation, smooth muscle relaxation and central nervous system and cardiac stimulation.
Inhibiting uric acid excretion is pyrazinamide's effect, which makes patients hyperuricemic; theophylline has a diuretic effect.

pubd2.io: Describe the molecular mechanism of action of drugs used for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
pubd2.q: In airway smooth muscle, the cyclic adenosine monophosphate produced after beta-2 receptor stimulation inhibits which enzyme?
opts: Phosphodiesterase is the enzyme theophylline inhibits, which raises cyclic adenosine monophosphate; in the beta-2 pathway cyclic adenosine monophosphate inhibits myosin light chain kinase.

Correct. The beta-2 receptor acts through the stimulatory G protein to make cyclic adenosine monophosphate, which inhibits myosin light chain kinase, so the myosin light chain is not phosphorylated and the muscle relaxes.
The phosphatase removes the phosphate from the myosin light chain, reversing the kinase step; cyclic adenosine monophosphate inhibits myosin light chain kinase itself.
5-lipoxygenase converts arachidonic acid toward the leukotrienes; the enzyme inhibited in the beta-2 pathway is myosin light chain kinase.

pubd2.io: Describe the molecular mechanism of action of drugs used for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
pubd2.q: How do ipratropium and tiotropium cause bronchodilation?
opts: Stimulating beta-2 receptors is how albuterol and salmeterol work, by increasing cyclic adenosine monophosphate; anticholinergics block muscarinic receptors.
Correct. Anticholinergics block acetylcholine's effect on muscarinic receptors, which produces bronchodilation.
Phosphodiesterase inhibition is theophylline's mechanism; ipratropium and tiotropium block acetylcholine at muscarinic receptors.
Mast cell stabilization is the action of cromolyn and nedocromil; ipratropium and tiotropium block acetylcholine at muscarinic receptors.

pubd2.io: Summarize side effects and toxic manifestations of respiratory drugs
pubd2.q: A patient develops flushing, fever, dry mouth and a fast heart rate after taking an anticholinergic. Which other finding belongs to the same toxicity pattern?
opts: Anticholinergic toxicity causes constipation, not diarrhea, along with urinary retention, flushing, fever and dry mouth.
The dry mouth already present rules this out: anticholinergics cause dry mouth and dry eyes; urinary retention fits the pattern.
ruled out by a stated finding
The fast heart rate already present rules this out: anticholinergic toxicity causes tachycardia and hypertension; urinary retention completes the pattern.
ruled out by a stated finding
Correct. Anticholinergic toxicity also affects the bowel and bladder, giving constipation and urinary retention, alongside flushing, fever, dry mouth and tachycardia.

pubd2.io: Identify respiratory drug classes and commonly prescribed drugs for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
pubd2.q: Ipratropium (Atrovent) belongs to which drug class?
opts: Correct. Ipratropium is the short-acting anticholinergic: it blocks acetylcholine's effect on muscarinic receptors, causing bronchodilation, and lasts up to 8 hours.
Beta-2 agonists such as albuterol increase cyclic adenosine monophosphate; ipratropium is an anticholinergic that blocks muscarinic receptors.
Methylxanthines such as theophylline are nonspecific phosphodiesterase inhibitors; ipratropium is an anticholinergic bronchodilator.
Mast cell stabilizers (cromolyn, nedocromil) must be taken before antigen exposure; ipratropium is an anticholinergic bronchodilator.

pubd2.io: Describe adverse effects of drugs used for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
pubd2.q: Which effect on the stomach is listed among theophylline's adverse effects?
opts: Blocking gastric acid secretion is what famotidine, a histamine H2 blocker, does; theophylline stimulates gastric acid.
Constipation belongs to anticholinergic toxicity; theophylline's listed effect on the stomach is stimulation of gastric acid.
Oral candidiasis is an inhaled corticosteroid adverse effect; theophylline's listed effect on the stomach is stimulation of gastric acid.
Correct. Theophylline stimulates gastric acid, and nausea and heartburn are on the methylxanthine adverse effect list.

pubd2.io: Describe adverse effects of drugs used for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
pubd2.q: Which pair of adverse effects is listed for beta-2 agonists as a class?
opts: Oral candidiasis and growth suppression in children are the inhaled corticosteroid adverse effects; beta-2 agonists cause increased heart rate and tremor.
Dry mouth and urinary retention belong to anticholinergic toxicity; the beta-2 agonist pair is increased heart rate and tremor.
Correct. Beta-2 agonists increase cyclic adenosine monophosphate and relax airway smooth muscle, but they cause increased heart rate and tremor.
Convulsions and arrhythmias are the dangers of high theophylline levels; beta-2 agonists cause increased heart rate and tremor.

pubd2.io: Describe the molecular mechanism of action of drugs used for pulmonary infections, asthma, and COPD/COLD
pubd2.q: Besides the direct effect of released mediators, stimulation of which airway receptors initiates reflex bronchoconstriction in asthma?
opts: Correct. Released mediators also stimulate afferent vagal receptors in the airways to initiate reflex bronchoconstriction, and tachykinins such as substance P directly contract smooth muscle.
Stimulating beta-2 receptors raises cyclic adenosine monophosphate and relaxes airway smooth muscle; reflex bronchoconstriction starts at afferent vagal receptors.
Adenosine A2B receptors are the ones theophylline antagonizes as part of its action; the reflex route of bronchoconstriction starts at afferent vagal receptors.
Immunoglobulin E receptors on mast cells trigger degranulation, the direct mediator route; the reflex route of bronchoconstriction begins at afferent vagal receptors.
